models_evaluated: AI-ECG convolutional neural network (residual, pretrained on congenital heart disease ECGs)

links.outcome: AI-ECG discrimination and calibration variation across external sites
links.effect: AUROC ranged 0.69 to 0.88 across five sites (A 0.87, B 0.88, C 0.82, D 0.74, E 0.69); three of five sites met criteria for miscalibration.
links.quote: Notably, there was variation observed in AUROC across centres, which ranged from 0.69 to 0.88 (AUROC Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82; D: 0.74, E: 0.69; see Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

links.outcome: Calibration after centre-specific Platt scaling at miscalibrated sites
links.effect: After within-centre calibration, model adequately calibrated with expected calibration error 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z P=0.25); uncalibrated model showed negative net benefit across all centres.
links.quote: After within-centre calibration, the model was adequately calibrated with expected calibration error of 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z test P = 0.25, Figure 2 ).

links.outcome: Performance at local sites versus aggregate; need for local verification
links.effect: Two of five sites had lower AUROC and three of five miscalibrated; authors conclude local verification of discrimination and calibration is required.
links.quote: Based on the extensive external validation performed in this study, we conclude that local verification of discrimination and calibration is required.

links.outcome: AUROC across subgroups by sex, race/ethnicity, and age
links.effect: No difference by sex (P=0.18) or race/ethnicity (P=1.0); lower AUROC in <22 years vs older (0.73 vs 0.85; P=0.005).
links.quote: There was lower performance in children and young adults <22 years old vs. older adults (AUROC 0.73 vs. 0.85; P = 0.005).

links.outcome: AI-ECG versus QRS duration model discrimination and net reduction in CMR
links.effect: AI-ECG AUROC 0.87 vs 0.78 for QRS duration; QRS model gave no net CMR reduction (-0.02) at 0.25 threshold.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence analysis of electrocardiograms outperformed QRS duration (AUROC 0.87 vs. 0.78, see Supplementary material online , Figure S3 ).

links.outcome: Calibration and net benefit of uncalibrated model across sites
links.effect: Miscalibration at one high-AUROC site (B); uncalibrated model showed negative net benefit when all centres considered.
links.quote: This shows that without proper consideration of calibration, a model may be harmful compared with the current standard of care when considered in the context of clinical risk tolerance.

links.outcome: Differences between training and external validation populations
links.effect: External cohort had higher outcome prevalence than training (57 vs 38% composite; P<0.001) and heterogeneity in race/ethnicity, age, subtype; authors link miscalibration to out-of-distribution prevalence and age.
links.quote: The aggregated external validation cohort had a higher prevalence of disease outcomes compared with the training site (34 vs. 23% for RVEDVi ≥ 160, 48 vs. 29% for RVESVi ≥ 80, 61 vs. 36% for RVEF < 47%, 51 vs. 35% for LVEF < 55%, 57 vs. 38% for composite of ≥2 criteria; P < 0.001 for all comparisons).

links.outcome: Performance in external multisite validation versus expected generalizability
links.effect: External validation across five sites revealed two sites with suboptimal discrimination, indicating that standard external validation may not ensure generalizability.
links.quote: The current standards could be inadequate to ensure truly generalizable performance, which warrants further examination across the breadth of AI-ECG applications.

models_evaluated: AI-ECG deep learning model for ventricular remodelling

links.outcome: stand-alone replacement risk
links.effect: At <25% risk, AI may delay but not replace CMR because of false negatives; sensitivity 92%, NPV 87%.
links.quote: For low-risk patients who have less than a 25% risk of having an actionable CMR abnormality, use of this test may delay (but not necessarily replace due to false negatives) the need for surveillance CMR by a year, with 92% sensitivity and 87% NPV.

links.outcome: external-site discrimination variation
links.effect: External site AUROCs ranged 0.69–0.88, with Sites D 0.74 and E 0.69.
links.quote: Notably, there was variation observed in AUROC across centres, which ranged from 0.69 to 0.88 (AUROC Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82; D: 0.74, E: 0.69; see Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

links.outcome: site calibration
links.effect: 3/5 centres were miscalibrated, tending to underestimate ventricular-remodelling risk.
links.quote: Three of five centres met criteria for miscalibration (Sites B, D, E; see Supplementary material online , Results ), with miscalibrated sites tending to underestimate the risk of ventricular remodelling (See Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

links.outcome: AI versus QRS duration
links.effect: AI-ECG outperformed QRS duration: AUROC 0.87 vs. 0.78.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence analysis of electrocardiograms outperformed QRS duration (AUROC 0.87 vs. 0.78, see Supplementary material online , Figure S3 ).

links.outcome: within-centre calibration
links.effect: Within-centre calibration produced expected calibration error 6.1% and Spiegelhalter Z P = 0.25.
links.quote: After within-centre calibration, the model was adequately calibrated with expected calibration error of 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z test P = 0.25, Figure 2 ).

links.outcome: site-level performance variation
links.effect: Site AUROCs varied from 0.69 to 0.88 across five external centres.
links.quote: Notably, there was variation observed in AUROC across centres, which ranged from 0.69 to 0.88 (AUROC Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82; D: 0.74, E: 0.69; see Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

links.outcome: demographic and site performance
links.effect: No sex/race difference; age and site differences, with 2/5 sites lower AUROC and 3/5 miscalibrated.
links.quote: There was no difference by sex or race/ethnicity, but there were differences by age and site, with two of five sites with lower AUROC than the others, and three of five sites met criteria for miscalibration, which improved after centre-specific calibration.

links.outcome: AUROC variation across external validation sites
links.effect: AUROC varied across centres from 0.69 to 0.88 (Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82, D: 0.74, E: 0.69).
links.quote: Notably, there was variation observed in AUROC across centres, which ranged from 0.69 to 0.88 (AUROC Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82; D: 0.74, E: 0.69; see Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

links.outcome: model calibration error after centre-specific recalibration
links.effect: After within-centre calibration, the model was adequately calibrated with an expected calibration error of 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z test P = 0.25).
links.quote: After within-centre calibration, the model was adequately calibrated with expected calibration error of 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z test P = 0.25, Figure 2 ).

links.outcome: model discrimination in younger versus older patients
links.effect: AUROC was significantly lower in children and young adults <22 years old compared with older adults (0.73 vs. 0.85; P = 0.005).
links.quote: There was lower performance in children and young adults <22 years old vs. older adults (AUROC 0.73 vs. 0.85; P = 0.005).
